title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
event_hint: KAP paradigm introduction: Knowledge Access Planning for LLM serving with GraphSpec implementation
problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: LLM serving backends receive only serialized prompts, losing structured knowledge priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, confidence signals) from upstream selection processes. This forces uniform full-context KV consumption regardless of actual knowledge importance, increasing latency and degrading throughput as contexts lengthen.
mechanism: Knowledge Access Planning (KAP) elevates structured knowledge priors to first-class execution artifacts through a universal intermediate representation (runtime access plan). The IR encodes selected knowledge units, runtime object mappings, logical positions, access policy, and verification policy. Instantiated as GraphSpec with Graph-RAG frontend and VLLM backend, using compiler-executor architecture to translate structured priors into KV access plans without altering model weights, training, or logical prompt semantics.

evidence.claim: GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K context length while maintaining answer quality comparable to full-context decoding
evidence.condition: 128K-token long-context QA workload, proposal-time KV access metric

evidence.claim: GraphSpec achieves 1.19x decode-throughput speedup at 128K context length versus full-context decoding, with absolute performance of 51.70 TPS versus 45.68 TPS baseline at 64K context
Evaluated on four NVIDIA A800 80GB GPUs with tensor parallelism 4 and bfloat16 execution across 4K-128K long-context SPIQA QA workloads
Quality measured via SPIQA multimodal QA benchmark with LLM-as-judge metric achieving 87.9% pass rate versus 86.0% baseline and 95% human-audit agreement
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 12 Table 1, PDF Page 14 Table 4

evidence.claim: KAP decouples physical KV consumption from prompt length through GraphSpec compiler-executor architecture connecting Graph-RAG frontend to VLLM backend without altering model weights or training
evidence.baseline: linear physical cost growth with context length
evidence.condition: Theoretical phase-boundary model validation, Graph-RAG+VLLM instantiation

evaluation_context: Long-context QA workloads spanning 4K to 128K token contexts. Knowledge-selection frontend uses Graph-RAG to produce structured priors (graph topology, ranked evidence). LLM serving backend uses VLLM v0.16.0 extended with GraphSpec. Hardware: four NVIDIA A800 80GB GPUs with tensor parallelism 4 and bfloat16 execution. Dataset: SPIQA multimodal QA benchmark grounded in scientific papers. Quality metric: LLM similarity with fact consistency (40%), information completeness (30%), logical structure (20%), expression quality (10%), validated by human audit with 95% agreement. Efficiency metrics: decode throughput (TPS), time-to-first-token (TTFT), retained-KV ratios. Batch size and concurrency settings not specified in supplement.
limitations: Evaluation limited to long-context QA workloads on SPIQA dataset; generalization to other task types (code generation, multi-turn dialogue, agentic workflows) not addressed. Verification/fallback overhead not quantified. Phase-boundary model presented but positive-speedup regime conditions not fully specified. GraphSpec is one concrete instantiation; KAP paradigm generality claimed but only Graph-RAG+VLLM combination demonstrated. Batch size and concurrency configuration not specified, limiting reproducibility. TTFT includes plan compilation overhead but prefills are preserved for all methods.
project_relevance: Directly addresses AI infra horizontal dynamics question: which systems/hardware changes affect end-to-end efficiency. KAP introduces execution-time planning layer between knowledge selection and LLM serving, reducing GPU memory bandwidth pressure and improving throughput for RAG systems. Hardware specifics now visible (A800 80GB, 4x TP=4, bfloat16) enabling infrastructure assessment. Absolute performance metrics (51.70 TPS vs 45.68 baseline, TTFT ~12.6s) provide concrete engineering boundaries. Quality validation via human audit (95% agreement) strengthens production relevance. Should be tracked as infra-level optimization paradigm; may warrant dedicated topic if adoption emerges in production serving stacks.
